name: Architectural Light → Circadian Entrainment Quality
mechanism_chain_provenance: NEWLY ESTABLISHED in LIGHT-I — gap stub only; no prior structural template

mechanism_chain.description: Building light environment: spectral composition + irradiance + timing schedule across 24h

data.finding: Building design determines spectral composition, irradiance levels, and timing of light exposure across occupancy period
data.effect: WFR, glazing, orientation determine daylight delivery

justification.backing: Architectural parameters directly control the light environment. This is the input layer of the circadian system.
justification.qualifier: Occupant behavior (shading use, outdoor breaks) modifies architectural delivery.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if behavioral factors dominate architectural effects.

mechanism_chain.description: → Daily melanopic lux integral (m-lux·hours) during photophase determines cumulative SCN phase-stabilization signal

data.finding: Minimum 150 m-lux·hours daily daytime melanopic dose for stable entrainment maintenance
data.effect: Below 100 m-lux·h: progressive drift; above 250: diminishing returns

justification.backing: The cumulative daily melanopic dose determines entrainment strength. Kronauer's model predicts entrainment as a function of light integral.
justification.qualifier: Minimum threshold derived from model extrapolation; direct measurement in occupied buildings is limited.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if light timing matters more than integral; or if individual chronotype dominates building effects.

mechanism_chain.description: → Evening melanopic lux above threshold (>30 m-lux) delays SCN phase via PRC delay region

data.finding: Evening light above 30 m-lux mEDI contributes to SCN delay region of PRC
data.effect: Threshold 30 m-lux in evening sensitivity window

justification.backing: The PRC delay region is activated by evening light. This partially offsets morning advance contributions.
justification.qualifier: Threshold varies with circadian phase; lower at peak sensitivity.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if evening light effects are acute only without cumulative phase-shifting.

mechanism_chain.description: → Net daily phase correction = advance contribution (morning light) minus delay contribution (evening light)

data.finding: Phase response curve integrates morning advance and evening delay contributions
data.effect: Net correction depends on timing-weighted light exposure

justification.backing: Kronauer's limit-cycle model formalizes the advance-delay integration.
justification.qualifier: Model validated in controlled conditions; architectural translation involves additional uncertainty.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if morning and evening contributions are not additive.

mechanism_chain.description: → If net correction ≥ intrinsic period deviation (0.17–0.22 h/day): stable entrainment maintained

data.finding: Human intrinsic circadian period averages 24.2h; requires 0.2h/day correction for entrainment

justification.backing: Stable entrainment requires daily phase correction to match the intrinsic period deviation.
justification.qualifier: Individual variation in intrinsic period affects minimum light requirement.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if non-photic zeitgebers (meals, activity) provide sufficient correction.

mechanism_chain.description: → If net correction < intrinsic period deviation: progressive phase drift → social jetlag → chronic misalignment

data.finding: Social jetlag (mismatch between biological and social clock) prevalent in modern populations; associated with inadequate daytime light exposure
data.effect: Social jetlag correlates with indoor work and low light exposure

justification.backing: Wittmann's social jetlag concept captures the cumulative misalignment that results from inadequate entrainment.
justification.qualifier: Epidemiological association; direct architectural causation is inferred.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if social jetlag is primarily driven by behavioral choices rather than architectural light.

mechanism_chain.description: → Chronic misalignment → allostatic load via cortisol CAR blunting, sleep architecture degradation (CB_SLEEP_ARCHITECTURE_002), metabolic dysregulation (Panda pathway)

data.finding: Circadian misalignment associated with metabolic syndrome, cognitive impairment, increased disease risk
data.effect: Multiple adverse outcomes from chronic misalignment

justification.backing: The health consequences of chronic misalignment are documented in shift-work and epidemiological literature. Panda's gene-expression pathway adds molecular mechanism.
justification.qualifier: Architectural extrapolation involves assumptions about equivalence between shift-work and inadequate-light misalignment.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if behavioral compensation eliminates architectural effects; or if misalignment effects are reversible with recovery periods.

luminance_level.note: Minimum cumulative daily daytime melanopic dose for stable entrainment maintenance. Equivalent to approximately 87 m-lux for 2 continuous hours, or 50 m-lux for 3–4 hours. Below 100 m-lux·h: progressive circadian drift expected over weeks. Above 250 m-lux·h: diminishing returns; ceiling effects in entrainment quality.
luminance_level.source: Kronauer model derivation; Figueiro et al. (2017) field data

evening_delay_contamination_threshold.note: Evening light above 30 m-lux mEDI in the 2 hours before habitual sleep onset begins contributing to the SCN delay region of the PRC, partially offsetting the morning advance contribution. This threshold is lower than the daytime maintenance threshold due to the circadian phase-dependent sensitivity of the SCN in the evening.
evening_delay_contamination_threshold.source: Arendt; Münch et al. (2006); Gooley et al. (2011)

social_setting_features.note: Rate of social jetlag accumulation in occupants working in buildings with daytime melanopic integral below the minimum threshold (150 m-lux·h/day). Each week of subthreshold exposure produces approximately 12 minutes of progressive phase delay. After 4 weeks: ~48 min delay; this represents the equivalent of living 1 time zone west of local clock time.
social_setting_features.source: Kronauer model projection; Wittmann et al. (2006) social jetlag epidemiology
social_setting_features.flag: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT — directly measured architectural accumulation rate absent; derived from free-running period × entrainment failure model

ie_dpt_interaction: No primary T_IE interaction; T_IE_001 secondary — occupant scheduling behavior (choosing indoor vs. outdoor breaks) modulates daily melanopic integral

cross_template_interactions.IC2: Primary interaction: social jetlag accumulation is a persistent body-budget phase-misalignment — the strongest IC2 interaction in the circadian template cluster. The body budget model generates predictions timed to clock time; when the circadian clock is phase-delayed from social schedule, the predictions systematically miss, producing a structural source of body-budget prediction error.
cross_template_interactions.AX4: Occupant control of break timing, lunch location (indoor vs. outdoor), and desk proximity to windows all modulate the daily melanopic integral. AX4 modifier: high control → occupant can compensate for subthreshold architectural delivery via outdoor exposure.

higher_order_principle: Building light environment → allostatic load pathway: The mechanism by which architectural light → circadian entrainment quality operates
